Statewide Cybersecurity Grants
SUMMARYOFFUNDS	FY 2025	FY 2026
	Actual	Estimate

FOOTNOTES

1/ The amount appropriated for the federal cybersecurity grant matching monies line item is exempt from section 35-190, Arizona Revised Statutes, relating to the lapsing of appropriations, until June 30, 2028. (FY 2026 General Appropriations Act footnote)

2/ Of the amount appropriated for statewide cybersecurity grants, the Arizona department of homeland security may spend up to \$500,000 for grant administration. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

3/ General Appropriations Act funds are appropriated as a Lump Sum with Special Line Items by Agency.

Cybersecurity Programs

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for cybersecurity programs. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Federal Cybersecurity Grant Matching Monies

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for Federal Cybersecurity Grant Matching Monies. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Federal Grant Match

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(107,800) from the General Fund in FY 2027 to eliminate one-time funding for a Federal Cybersecurity Grant Match.

As part of the Federal Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security created the State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP). The goal of SLCGP is to assist state, local, and tribal governments with managing and reducing systemic cybersecurity risks. This line item provides the necessary state matching monies to draw down approximately \$5,000,000 in federal SLCGP funding.

To receive monies under the SLCGP, a state must 1) establish a “Cybersecurity Planning Committee” that can organize statewide cybersecurity efforts and 2) develop a cybersecurity plan that addresses the entire jurisdiction and incorporates cybersecurity best practices. Federal grant requirements stipulate that the department must pass through at least 80% of the grant funding to local governments, with at least 25% of the 80% benefiting rural areas with populations of 50,000 or less.

The FY 2026 budget included an appropriation of \$107,800 for this line item, which is exempt from lapsing through FY 2028.

Multi-factor Authentication

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for Multi-Factor Authentication technologies. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(550,000) from the IT Fund in FY 2027 to eliminate one-time funding for multifactor authentication technologies.

Arizona State Nonprofit Security Grant Program Fund Deposit

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for an Arizona State Nonprofit Security Grant Program Fund Deposit. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The FY 2024 Criminal Justice Budget Reconciliation Bill (BRB) established the non-appropriated Nonprofit Security Grant Program Fund to provide safety and security grants for projects at nonprofit organizations that are at a high risk of terrorist attacks or hate crimes. The FY 2024 budget included a one-time deposit of \$5,000,000 from the General Fund into the fund. The FY 2025 Criminal Justice BRB limited grant eligibility to those entities that have not received federal funding for the last 3 cycles and establishes a review panel to ensure eligibility.

The line item funds a grant program to provide eligible nonprofits with safety and security grants. The department shall award up to \$1,000,000 in each of FY 2025 – FY 2028 and a nonprofit may not receive more than \$100,000 in any grant year. Priority shall be given to organizations that are unable to apply for other funding. A budget footnote allows the department to spend up to

5% of the monies deposited in the fund to administer the grant program.

As of June 30, 2025, the department had distributed \$1,614,100, from this allocation. These monies are exempt from lapsing.

Statewide Information Security and Privacy Operations and Controls

The Baseline includes \$11,145,200 and 26 FTE Positions from the Information Technology (IT) Fund in FY 2027 for Statewide Information Security and Privacy Operations and Controls. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

Remove One-Time Funding

The Statewide Information Security and Privacy Office (SISPO) in the department performs strategic planning, policy development, risk assessment, facilitation, and coordination to protect the state’s information resources. The IT Fund receives revenue from a 0.61% pro-rata charge on agency payroll.

Statewide Cybersecurity Grants

The Baseline includes \$10,000,000 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for Statewide Cybersecurity Grants. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The line item funds a grant program to provide local political subdivisions with resources for cybersecurity readiness and tools. A budget footnote allows the department to use up to \$500,000 of the appropriation to administer the grant program.

Arizona State Nonprofit Security Grant Program Fund (HLA8888/Laws 2023, Chapter Non-Appropriated 137)

Source of Revenue: Grants, gifts, donations and legislative appropriations.

Purpose of Fund: To provide funding for safety and security projects to nonprofit organizations that are at high risk of a terrorist attack or at risk of hate crimes or attacks because of the nonprofit's ideology, beliefs or mission for target hardening and other security enhancements and activities. General Fund appropriation expenditures are not displayed to avoid double counting of appropriations.

Funds Expended 0 0

Federal Funds (HLA2000/A.R.S. § 41-4254)

Federal Funds

Source of Revenue: Grants received from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

Purpose of Fund: To provide state agencies and local governments with funding to deter and mitigate acts of terrorism. Federal grant guidelines allow up to 5% of the grand total to be used for administrative costs.

Information Technology Fund (HLA2152/A.R.S. § 18-401) Appropriated

Source of Revenue: A pro rata share of 0.61% of total payroll, charged to all budget units subject to oversight of information technology projects by ADOA’s Arizona Strategic Enterprise Technology (ASET) Office or by the Information Technology Authorization Committee (ITAC).

Purpose of Fund: Monies from the Information Technology (IT) Fund support the operation of the Statewide Information Security and Privacy Office (SISPO). Monies also provide personnel funding for statewide IT planning, coordinating, oversight, and consulting at the Arizona Department of Administration.
